title: cmate-orchestrate merge report v1
description: Report printed to stdout and written to merge-report.json by the cmate-orchestrate merge runner (scripts/merge.mjs). Closed schema: an unknown field is a contract violation, not something a reader may ignore. It records one mutating phase — either PR creation (create_prs) or guarded merge (merge_prs) — over the verification-passed issues of an already-executed plan. A single invocation enables exactly one phase. Nothing is created or merged without explicit approval, and no PR is merged unless its CI passed; a create failure, a red or pending CI, or a merge conflict stops the phase and is reported as partial, never rounded up to success. Every property is required EXCEPT integration_verify, which exists only in a run that opted into --integration-verify (Issue #175) — a report written without that flag carries the same key set, and the same bytes, as it did before the field existed.

phase.description: The single mutating phase this invocation enabled. create_prs opens a PR per verification-passed issue; merge_prs checks CI and, if green and approved, merges. Exactly one is ever enabled.

status.description: success: the phase handled every eligible issue without a failure (including a no-mutation preview). partial: the phase started but stopped early on a PR-create failure, a red/pending CI, a missing PR, or a merge conflict. failure: nothing could be attempted (preflight failed, no plan, or a bad invocation).

stop_reason.description: Why the phase stopped. completed: every eligible issue was handled. The rest name the first blocking condition; a failure is never reported as completed. No value was added for the integration verification of Issue #175: a red merged state lands on merge_failed and a requested-but-impossible verification on merge_failed (after the merges) or preflight_failed (refused before them), with blocking_reasons[].code — integration_verify_failed / integration_verify_unavailable — naming what actually happened. ci_failed and ci_pending deliberately do NOT receive it: in this report those two mean 'a PR was not merged because its CI was not green', and an integration failure happens after successful merges.

approved.description: Whether --approve was given. When false the phase is a no-mutation preview: no branch is pushed, no PR is created, and no PR is merged.

mutated.description: Whether at least one mutating command (git push, gh pr create, or gh pr merge) was actually invoked. Always false when approved is false.

merge_method.description: The merge method used (or that would be used) for the merge_prs phase. Reported in both phases for completeness.

out_dir.description: Directory the merge artifacts were written to. Null when nothing was written.

eligible_issues.description: Issues drawn from the dispatch report whose worker completed AND whose verification passed. Only these are ever acted on: an unverified issue is never turned into a PR or a merge.

preflight.description: Read-only preflight probes run before any mutation (gh availability, repo access, base resolvable). A blocking failure yields status failure and nothing is attempted.

targets.description: One record per eligible issue, in merge order. A target reached after the phase stopped is recorded with outcome skipped so the full set stays visible.

integration_verify.description: Present only when --integration-verify was passed (merge_prs only, Issue #175). The wave barrier's second half: after every merge this invocation performed, the profile's post-merge verification set is run on the MERGED state of the base branch — fetched from origin and checked out into a throwaway detached worktree, so the invocation's own working tree is never touched. The set is plan.profile.integration_baseline ?? plan.profile.baseline, resolved on the KEY'S PRESENCE (Issue #195), and `source` records which one ran. Absent means the run did not verify the merged state; it never means the merged state is green.

requested.description: Always true: the object exists only because --integration-verify was passed.

ran.description: Whether the baseline commands were actually executed on the merged checkout. False with outcome not_run means nothing measured the merged state.

outcome.description: pass: every profile baseline command exited 0 on the merged base. fail: one exited non-zero — the state the merges add up to is red even though each PR's own CI was green on a base that did not yet contain the others (integration_verify_failed). not_run: nothing was merged in this invocation, or the verification could not be performed (integration_verify_not_run / integration_verify_unavailable). not_run is never green. The next wave is dispatched only when the run is a success AND this is pass — this outcome adds a condition, it does not replace the status check.

base.description: The profile's base ref, transcribed. What to run and where to run it both come from the profile; no branch name and no toolchain is hardcoded in the runner.

base_sha.description: Short SHA of the fetched base tip that was verified, or null when it could not be read.

merged_issues.description: The issues whose PRs THIS invocation merged — the merges whose combined result is being judged. Empty means the base branch did not move here.

source.description: WHICH profile field the commands below came from (Issue #195). integration_baseline: the profile declares that field, and it is what ran — the repository's definition of a green merged branch, which is generally heavier than what each worker runs. baseline: the profile does not declare integration_baseline, so the worker health-check list ran as the fallback (the pre-#195 behaviour, unchanged for every profile that does not declare the field). Recorded on the paths that ran nothing too, because a refusal for a DECLARED-empty integration_baseline and a refusal for a profile with no baseline at all have opposite next actions. Without this field the split would be a silent second baseline: two reports that measured different sets read identically.

commands.description: The commands of the field named by `source`, transcribed in profile order. Empty means that field supplies none — an absent/empty `baseline`, or an `integration_baseline` declared as [] (which states that the repository has no integration verification and is NOT answered with `baseline`) — and either way it is refused before the first merge rather than skipped.

failed_command.description: The first baseline command that exited non-zero, or null.

exit_code.description: That command's exit status, or null when it could not be captured.

eligible.description: True: this issue's worker completed and its verification passed. Only eligible issues appear as targets.

pushed.description: Whether the branch was pushed (create_prs phase only; always false in a preview or in merge_prs).

ci_passed.description: Whether every required check reported success. A merge is refused unless this is true — completion never opens the merge gate on its own.
